'''Jan Veselý''' (born 24 April 1990) is a Czech former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|m=2.10}},<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=000925&seasoncode=E2016 VESELY, JAN HEIGHT: 2.13]</ref><ref>[http://www.fenerbahce.org/basketbolerkek/detay.asp?ContentID=41852&lang=eng Name: JAN VESELY Height: 2.10 m]</ref> he played both the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] positions. He was selected sixth overall in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Washington Wizards]]. Veselý is a Three-time [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] selection.

==Professional career==
===Early years===
Veselý began playing basketball with the youth clubs of Příbor and BK Snakes Ostrava in the Czech Republic. In 2007, he moved to Slovenia and signed with [[KD Slovan|Geoplin Slovan]].

===Partizan (2008–2011)===
In April 2008, he signed a multi-year deal with Serbian club [[KK Partizan|Partizan]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Veseli pristupio Partizanu|url=http://www.srbijasport.com/vest.php?news_id=12058&sport_id=21|access-date=15 May 2015|work=srbijasport.com|date=5 May 2008|language=sr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808002733/http://www.srbijasport.com/vest.php?news_id=12058&sport_id=21|archive-date=8 August 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He won nine club trophies with the club,<ref name="Mondo3">[[Mondo Media|Mondo]]: [http://www.mondo.rs/s208673/Sport/Sport/Kosarka/Pitajte_Jana_Veselog.html Pitajte Jana Veselog] {{in lang|sr}} (10 June 2011)</ref> and also reached the [[2009–10 Euroleague Final Four]]. In 2010, Veselý was presented the [[FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Vesely Voted Young Men's Player Of The Year|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_5LlHwLsVG42hTNoLSGSOo0.coid_dHPWomBiHJgwYHWWOnMb83.articleMode_on.html|access-date=15 May 2015|work=fibaeurope.com|date=14 February 2011}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2011–2014)===
Veselý was drafted in the first round by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the sixth overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Irving goes No. 1 to Cleveland|url=http://www.nba.com/draft/2011/|work=NBA.com|access-date=31 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525070935/http://www.nba.com/draft/2011/|archive-date=25 May 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> After [[Flip Saunders]] was fired, Veselý saw more minutes on the court under new coach [[Randy Wittman]], who also implored him to be more aggressive offensively.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jan Vesely: Forward aims to get better with the ball |website=The Washington Times |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2012/oct/17/jan-vesely-randy-wittman-expects-more-wizards-forw/ |date=October 17, 2012 |access-date=March 23, 2025}}</ref> On April 9th, 2012, he recorded his first double-double, finishing the game with 11 points and 11 rebounds in a win over the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Wizards get 67 points from bench, blister Bobcats|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320409030|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120413231959/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320409030|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 April 2012|access-date=15 May 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|date=10 April 2012}}</ref> Veselý continued his success over the Bobcats on April 23rd, when he posted a career-high 16 points on 8-8 shooting.<ref>{{cite news|title=Wizards paste Bobcats for first 4-game win streak since 2007|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320423027|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426214206/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320423027|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 April 2012|access-date=15 May 2015|work=[[ESPN]]|date=24 April 2012}}</ref> He averaged 4.7 points and 4.4 rebounds in his first NBA season. However, in his second season with the Wizards, he averaged just 2.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game, while shooting just 31% from the free-throw line. He continued to struggle in his third year with the Wizards. Playing in 33 games, he averaged 3.2 points and 3.4 rebounds per game, and shot only 27% from the free-throw line.

===Denver Nuggets (2014)===
On 20 February 2014, Veselý was traded to the Denver Nuggets in a three-team trade.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-acquire-jan-vesely-washington Denver Nuggets Acquire Jan Vesely From Washington]</ref> Until the end of the season, he appeared in 21 games, averaging 4.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and a career-high 1.3 steals per game.

===Fenerbahçe (2014–2022)===
On 5 August 2014, Veselý signed a two-year deal with the Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce Ulker lands high flier Vesely|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/139764/180|access-date=6 August 2014|work=Euroleague.net|date=5 August 2014}}</ref>

Fenerbahçe advanced to the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four]], the first time in the team's history that they played in a [[EuroLeague Final Four]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce for the first time in the Final Four|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/2015/04/league-action/87436/|access-date=15 May 2015|work=eurohoops.net|date=20 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518101508/http://www.eurohoops.net/2015/04/league-action/87436/|archive-date=18 May 2015}}</ref> On 15 May 2015, however, they lost in the EuroLeague semifinal game to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], by a score of 87–96.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid heads to third straight final after beating Fenerbahce|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=248&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=15 May 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=15 May 2015}}</ref> Veselý contributed with 20 points and 6 rebounds in the semifinal game. Eventually, Fenerbahçe finished in 4th place in the EuroLeague, after losing in the third-place game to [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], by a score of 80–86.<ref>{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow beats Fenerbahce in third-place game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=18 May 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> Over 29 EuroLeague games played in the 2014–15 season, he averaged a career-high 11.2 points and 5.4 rebounds per game, on 63.3% shooting from the field.

He was the [[EuroLeague]]'s [[Fenerbahçe Ülker Euroleague 2015–16|2015–16]] season selection as the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month|MVP for the month of January]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6ni8o9q57yy8hsdc MVP for January: Jan Vesely, Fenerbahce Istanbul]</ref><ref>[http://www.fenerbahce.org/detay.asp?ContentID=48822 Jan Vesely won Euroleague 2015-16 January MVP]</ref> On 21 March 2016, it was announced that he would be sidelined for up to six weeks, due to an [[Achilles tendon rupture|Achilles tendon]] injury, which caused him to miss the entire EuroLeague playoffs against [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce's Vesely sidelined through playoffs|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6rg8bktgtli6bepy/fenerbahce-s-vesely-sidelined-through-playoffs|access-date=13 April 2016|work=euroleague.net|date=21 March 2016}}</ref> He'd make his return on 13 May 2016, in the [[2016 Euroleague Final Four|2016 Final Four]] match-up against [[Saski Baskonia|Laboral Kutxa]]. In his return, he'd record 14 points, in an 88–77 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] victory against them, while also being announced as a part of the [[All-EuroLeague]] First Team, for his performances in the 2015–16 Euroleague season, before his Achilles tendon injury.
[[File:2021-10-12 ALBA Berlin gegen Fenerbahçe SK (EuroLeague 2021-22) by Sandro Halank–040.jpg|thumb|right|150 px|Veselý with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] in 2021]]
On 9 July 2016, Veselý signed a new three-year contract with Fenerbahçe, with NBA opt-out clauses every summer.<ref>{{cite news|title=Vesely signed with Fenerbahce until 2019|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/featured/277842/vesely-signed-with-fenerbahce-until-2019|access-date=9 July 2016|work=Eurohoops.net|date=9 July 2016}}</ref> In 2017, Fenerbahçe defeated Olympiakos 80–64 in the Euroleague final in Istanbul, becoming the champion for the first time in its history and Veselý became one of the most important parts of that Fenerbahçe basketball team.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/spor-39995475#:~:text=Olympiakos'u%2080%2D64%20yenen,de%C4%9Ferli%20oyuncusu%20(MVP)%20se%C3%A7ildi|title=Fenerbahçe Basketbol Takımı Avrupa Şampiyonu|newspaper=BBC News Türkçe}}</ref> In May 2018, he was named the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] for the [[2017–18 EuroLeague|2017–18 season]], his second career nomination.<ref name="all-euroleague">{{cite news|title=2017-18 All-EuroLeague First Team presented by 7DAYS|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8q8jd3dq5w55m5ab/2017-18-all-euroleague-first-team-presented-by-7days|access-date=19 May 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=10 May 2018}}</ref> In [[2017–18 EuroLeague]], Fenerbahçe made it to the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four]], its fourth consecutive Final Four appearance. Eventually, they lost to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] with 80–85 in the final game.<ref name="EuroLeague18Champ">{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is 2018 EuroLeague champion|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=260&seasoncode=E2017#!report|access-date=20 May 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=20 May 2018}}</ref> Over 34 EuroLeague games, he averaged career-highs of 12.5 points and 1.6 assists, while also having 5.1 rebounds per game.

On 18 February 2019, Veselý signed a three-year contract extension with Fenerbahçe.<ref name="2019extension">{{cite news |title=Vesely stays at Fenerbahce through 2022 |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9h3ysh55rqije9ch/vesely-stays-at-fenerbahce-through-2022 |access-date=18 February 2019 |work=euroleague.net |date=18 February 2019}}</ref> On 9 May 2019, Veselý was once again named to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]].<ref>{{cite news |title=2018-19 All-EuroLeague First Team presented by 7DAYS |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9nhvy8y5s6sg8pkv/2018-19-all-euroleague-first-team-presented-by-7days |access-date=18 May 2019 |work=euroleague.net |date=9 May 2019}}</ref> Later that month, Veselý was named the [[EuroLeague MVP]] for [[2018–19 EuroLeague]] season.<ref name="elmvp2019">{{cite news |title=2018-19 Season MVP: Jan Vesely, Fenerbahce Beko Istanbul |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9oa9uqukt67j7p89/2018-19-season-mvp-jan-vesely-fenerbahce-beko-istanbul |access-date=18 May 2019 |work=euroleague.net}}</ref>

On 21 June 2022, Veselý officially parted ways with the Turkish club after eight seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2022/6/formamiza-iz-birakanlar-unutulmazlar%E2%80%A6%E2%80%9D-jan-vesely-ye-sonsuz-tesekkurlerimizle|title="Formamıza iz bırakanlar unutulmazlar…" Jan Vesely'ye Sonsuz Teşekkürlerimizle|last=|first=|date=21 June 2022|website=|publisher=[[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]]|language=tr|access-date=21 June 2022}}</ref>

===FC Barcelona (2022–2026)===
On 1 July 2022, Veselý signed a three-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Basquet|FC Barcelona]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fc-barcelona-announced-jan-vesely/|title=FC Barcelona announced Jan Vesely|last=|first=|date=1 July 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=1 July 2022|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref> In April 2023, he became the EuroLeague's all-time leader in 2-pointers made, with 1,293 shots made in total.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jan Vesely becomes an all-time EuroLeague leader in 2-pointers made |url=https://basketnews.com/news-188873-jan-vesely-becomes-an-all-time-euroleague-leader-in-2-pointers-made.html|date=29 April 2023|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=basketnews.com}}</ref> In his first season with the Catalans, Veselý won the [[2022–23 ACB season|2022–23 Liga ACB]] and helped the team reach the [[2023 EuroLeague Final Four]].<ref>{{cite web|title=¡Un Barça colosal conquista la Liga Endesa 2022-23! (82-93)
 |url=https://www.acb.com/es/supercopa/noticias/un-barca-colosal-conquista-la-liga-endesa-2022-23-82-93-138619|date=20 June 2023|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=acb.com|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Road to Final Four: FC Barcelona
 |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/news/eb22-23-f4-road-to-final-four-fc-barcelona/|date=15 May 2023|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]}}</ref>

On May 12, 2026, Veselý announced his retirement from professional basketball at the end of the 2025–26 season.<ref name="retirement2026">{{cite news |title=Jan Vesely announces retirement at end of season |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4502645/jan-vesely-announces-retirement-at-end-of-season |access-date=16 May 2026 |work=fcbarcelona.com |date=12 May 2026}}</ref> At the time of the announcement, he was among the [[EuroLeague career statistical leaders|EuroLeague's statistical leaders]] in several categories.<ref>{{cite web|first=Javier|last=Gancedo|title=Jan Vesely retires as a pillar of the EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/jan-vesely-retires-as-a-pillar-of-the-euroleague/|date=12 May 2026|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]}}</ref>

==National team career==
Veselý has been a member of the senior men's [[Czech Republic national basketball team]], having previously played for the Czech Republic's junior national teams. He has played at the [[EuroBasket 2013]] and the [[EuroBasket 2015]].

On 31 July 2021, Veselý scored 13 points in a loss to the [[United States men's national basketball team]] at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in Tokyo, Japan.

==Playing style==
Prior to the [[2011 NBA Draft]], Veselý was compared to [[National Basketball Association#International influence|European NBA superstars]] [[Dirk Nowitzki]] and [[Andrei Kirilenko]] due to his speed and court movement.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Draft 2011: Jan Vesely and 5 Best Prospects for the Washington Wizards |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/741197-nba-draft-2011-jan-vesely-and-5-best-prospects-for-the-washington-wizards|date=23 June 2011|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Washout no longer? Czech Republic's Jan Vesely intrigues scouts once again |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13683878/nba-washington-wizards-washout-jan-vesely-excels-eurobasket-not-eager-nba-return|date=18 September 2015|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> Veselý himself compared his game to Nowitzki's in interviews.<ref name=slam>{{cite web|title=Jan Vesely: ‘I will enter the NBA Draft’ |url=https://slamonline.com/nba/jan-vesely-i-will-enter-the-nba-draft/|date=14 January 2011|access-date=12 May 2026|website=slamonline.com}}</ref> He was also compared to [[Blake Griffin]] due to his athleticism.<ref name=slam></ref>

While at the start of his career he was known for his size, athleticism, physicality and his ability to finish close to the rim, Veselý developed his mid-range shot into a trademark of his game over the years.<ref>{{cite web|title=
Jan Vesely's transfer grade: will he become Barca's answer to Tavares?|url=https://basketnews.com/news-174713-jan-veselys-transfer-grade-will-he-become-barcas-answer-to-tavares.html|date=6 July 2022|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=basketnews.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Javier|last=Gancedo|title=Jan Vesely is still adding more strings to his bow at 34 |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/jan-vesely-is-still-adding-more-strings-to-his-bow-at-34/|date=8 November 2024|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]}}</ref> By the latter years of his career, Veselý also added [[Three-point field goal|three-point shooting]] to his skillset.<ref>{{cite web|first=José Ignacio|last=Huguet|title=La nueva amenaza táctica del Barça: el triple de Jan Vesely |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/baloncesto/20260330/1004162244/nueva-amenaza-tactica-barca-triple-jan-vesely.html|date=20 June 2023|access-date=12 May 2026|publisher=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es}}</ref>

=== Free Throw Struggles and Turnaround ===
[[File:Jan Veselý 6 FC Barcelona (basketball) Euroleague 20251223 (6).jpg|thumb|right|200 px|Veselý shooting a [[free throw]] in 2025]]
One of the notable story lines of Vesely's career was his turnaround in free throw shooting. In his first year in the NBA, he memorably [[air ball|airballed]] his first free throw attempt,<ref name="EuroHeroes">{{cite web |title=The NBA Player Who Was SCARED of the Free Throw Line |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XOrDE14jiGw |website=youtube.com |publisher=EuroHeroes |language=en |format=video |date= 16 September 2023|access-date=9 August 2025}}</ref> then went on to shoot 53% for the season, in a league where the average was 75%. In his second year he shot 31%, and in his third year 27%. He admitted that the free throw problems were "a mental thing" and a lack of confidence.<ref name="EuroHoops">{{cite web|title=How Jan Vesely became one of EuroLeague’s top free throw shooters|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/trademarks/790142/how-jan-vesely-became-one-of-euroleagues-top-free-throw-shooters/|access-date=9 August 2025|last=Stroggylakis|first=Antonis|publisher=Eurohoops.net|date=10 December 2018}}</ref> His fear of shooting free throws was known to his teammates, and in one instance teammate [[Jordan Crawford]] attempted to shoot Vesely's free throws for him when Vesely had been fouled.<ref name="washpost">{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Steinberg|title=Remembering Jan Vesely|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/dc-sports-bog/wp/2014/02/20/remembering-jan-vesely/|access-date=9 August 2025|publisher=Washington Post|date=20 February 2014}}</ref> On discovering the switch, the referee took away the point that Crawford had made and gave the ball to Vesely, who then missed both free throws. His career 40.8% average in the NBA places him among some of the worst free throw shooters of all time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Player with the worst free throw percentage ever in NBA history|url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/player-with-the-worst-free-throw-percentage-ever-in-nba-history|access-date=9 August 2025|publisher=statemuse.com}}</ref>

On returning to Europe, Vesely continued to shoot less than 50% from the free throw line in [[EuroLeague]] play, and in the 2016 Final only made 1 from 10 free throws. His coach of the time, [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] coach [[Željko Obradović]], told him: "Even if you shoot 0 from 20 right now... I won’t care. The most important thing is for you to understand that it’s a completely psychological thing. That you need to go to the line and shoot as always you do because your form is very good." From that low point Vesely steadily gained confidence and improved.<ref name="EuroHoops"/>

Starting from the 2017–18 season, he almost consistently averaged over 70% shooting from the free throws. In three years playing for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] between 2022 and 2025, he averaged 78.1%. His transformation of what was one of the weakest parts of his game into one of his strengths was cited as an inspiration to teammates.<ref name="EuroHoops"/>

==Personal life==
Veselý was born on 24 April 1990 in [[Ostrava]] ([[Czechoslovakia]] then, [[Czech Republic]] now). His father, Jan, is a former basketball player, and his mother a former [[volleyball]] player.<ref name="Sportal">Sportal.rs: [http://www.sportal.rs/news.php?id=20552 Jan Veseli: Od Duleta sam mnogo naučio] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100516163514/http://www.sportal.rs/news.php?id=20552 |date=16 May 2010 }} {{in lang|sr}} (7 February 2010)</ref> Veselý's younger sister<ref name="Kapija">eKapija.com: [http://www.ekapija.com/website/sr/page/312840 Jan Vesely, košarkaš Partizana – veselje se širi na sve strane] {{in lang|sr}} (7 May 2010)</ref> is a basketball player.<ref name="Mondo5">[[Mondo Media|Mondo]]: [http://www.mondo.rs/s209292/Sport/Sport/Kosarka/Veseli_srecan_ti_put.html Veseli, srećan ti put!] {{in lang|sr}} (16 June 2011)</ref> Reportedly, he is fluent in [[Czech language|Czech]], [[Slovenian language|Slovenian]], [[Serbian language|Serbian]] and [[English language|English]].<ref name="Sport"/>

Veselý was a favorite of the [[Grobari|Partizan supporters]].<ref name="Vesti">Vesti.com: [http://www.vesti-online.com/Sport/Kosarka/109140/Lepo-mu-u-Beogradu-pa-ne-zuri-u-Ameriku Lepo mu u Beogradu, pa ne žuri u Ameriku] {{in lang|sr}} (9 January 2011)</ref> He stated he was "surprised by his popularity in Serbia, as no one in Czech Republic knew who he was".<ref name="Sport">''Sport'': [http://www.sport.novosti.rs/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=6580:jan-veseli-u-ekoj-ne-znaju-ko-sam&catid=98:jadranska-ligank&Itemid=131 Jan Veseli: U Češkoj ne znaju ko sam] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307062444/http://www.sport.novosti.rs/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=6580:jan-veseli-u-ekoj-ne-znaju-ko-sam&catid=98:jadranska-ligank&Itemid=131 |date=7 March 2012 }} {{in lang|sr}} (15 February 2010)</ref><ref name="Press">''[[Press (Belgrade newspaper)|Press]]'': [http://www.pressonline.rs/sr/vesti/sport/story/115750/Jan+Veseli%3A+Pove%C5%A1%C4%87u+celu+familiju+u+Pariz!.html Jan Veseli: Povešću celu familiju u Pariz] {{in lang|sr}} (5 May 2010)</ref> The Partizan supporters created two joke slogans, "When Jan plays, we are all joyful" ([[Serbian language|Serbian]]: "Kad Jan igra, svi smo veseli") and "We are all happy, only Jan is joyful" (Serbian: "Svi smo srećni, samo se Jan Veseli"), as his surname means "joyful" in both [[Czech language|Czech]] and Serbian.<ref name="Kurir2">''[[Kurir]]'': [http://www.kurir-info.rs/sport/jan-veseli-rasic-uz-dzordana-68518.php Jan Veseli: Rašić uz Džordana] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309131036/http://www.kurir-info.rs/sport/jan-veseli-rasic-uz-dzordana-68518.php |date=9 March 2012 }} {{in lang|sr}} (8 January 2011)</ref>

After the end of the 2010–11 season, which had been confirmed to be his last in Partizan, Veselý stated, "My first destination in Europe will always be Belgrade. Partizan, Belgrade and Serbia have given me a great opportunity, which now I can continue in another place. Serbia has become my second home".<ref name="Mondo2">[[Mondo Media|Mondo]]: [http://www.mondo.rs/s208749/Sport/Sport/Kosarka/Veseli_u_MONDU-_Iz_Amerike_-_pravac_Beograd.html Veseli u Mondu: Iz Amerike – pravac Beograd] {{in lang|sr}} (10 June 2011)</ref> He also added he would like to wear number 24 once again and that his wish was to end his career in Partizan.<ref name="Mondo2"/><ref name="SMedia2">S Media.com: [http://www.smedia.rs/sport/vest/47753/jan-veseli-kk-partizan-Veseli-Kraj-karijere-u-dresu-Partizana.html Veseli: Kraj karijere u dresu Partizana] {{in lang|sr}} (10 June 2011)</ref> Years of life in Serbia have left a permanent trace on his musical taste, as he said he likes [[Music of Serbia|Serbian music]] better than American or Czech music.<ref name="The Washington Post">The Washington Post: [https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/dc-sports-bog/post/jan-vesely-meets-the-dc-media/2011/06/27/AGO6LWnH_blog.html Jan Vesely meets the D.C. media] {{in lang|en}} (27 June 2011)</ref>

Veselý is a favorite of the [[Fenerbahçe S.K.#Supporters|Fenerbahçe supporters]] as well, with a slogan going "Jan Jan Vesely, let's fly Vesely, I can't help dunking!" ([[Turkish language|Turkish]]: "Jan Jan Vesely, uçalım Vesely, smacı basmadan duramıyorum!").<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NJGUrp_98TE Fenerbahçe taraftarından Jan Vesely'e özel şarkı]</ref>

One of Vesely's notable moments as a Wizard was a kiss he shared with then-girlfriend Eva Kodouskova on live television when he was drafted on June 23, 2011.<ref name="washpost"/> It became a minor Internet sensation,<ref>{{cite web|first=Jason|last=McIntyre|url=https://www.thebiglead.com/posts/jan-vesely-and-his-girlfriend-eva-kodouskova-were-the-nba-draft-s-biggest-winners-01dxe90g7pkk|title=Jan Vesely and His Girlfriend, Eva Kodouskova Were the NBA Draft's Biggest Winners|access-date=10 August 2025|date=24 June 2011|publisher=thebiglead.com}}</ref> and three years later the [[Washington Post]] referred to "The Kiss" as "the most memorable moment of Vesely's time" in Washington.
